scope: New /translators/ portrait gallery: 24 cards, modals with verbatim bio-corpus highlights, bidirectional links (atlas records + analysis pages), GA events. Page-authored copy three-agent reviewed; corpus excerpts machine-verified verbatim (144).

roles.focus: copy accuracy (caught: 'twenty-four lives' wrong — Butcher-Lang is two people)
final copy — kicker 'Twenty-four translations, one poem.', honest plaque accounting in lede+method note

decision: Arbiter blocks applied verbatim to the generator; verify-translators.mjs green.

trpage-r1.scope: Authored copy only: kicker, h1, lede, CTA panel, and Sources and rights note. Corpus excerpts were not reviewed.

blocks.original: Twenty-four lives spent on one poem
blocks.reason: The gallery has 24 translation records, not 24 individual lives: the Butcher–Lang record represents two people and the Pope record names Pope, Fenton, and Broome.

blocks.original: Every Odyssey in Skald was somebody's years of work — a philosopher, a rebel novelist, a court tutor, a war poet. Open a portrait to see who they were, how they came to Homer, and what their translation gave the poem. 19 of the twenty-four have public-domain portraits; the rest are still hiding from the archives.
blocks.replacement: Each Odyssey in Skald is the work of a translator—or, in two cases, a collaboration. Open a card to meet the people behind it, see their path to Homer, and learn about the translation. Nineteen of the twenty-four cards use portraits with a recorded public-domain basis; five use plaques: three because no locatable public-domain portrait was found, and two because U.S. public-domain status remains unconfirmed in the research.
blocks.reason: The original collapses 24 records into 24 lives; its occupational examples are not all supported by the reviewed corpus; and its archive metaphor hides the material distinction between three unavailable portraits and two withheld for unresolved U.S. public-domain status. The 19/5 split is verified.

blocks.original: Read them side by side. Skald sets all twenty-four beside the Greek, with the voyage map, the art, and the margins alive.
blocks.replacement: Read them side by side. Skald sets all twenty-four beside the Greek, with the voyage map, the art, and the margins alive.
blocks.reason: The bundled Odyssey content contains 24 translation records and the reader provides Greek/parallel reading, voyage-map, art, and margin-note features. “Alive” is plainly figurative.

blocks.original: Sources and rights. Biography highlights come from Skald's three-agent-reviewed translator research; portrait files are public-domain reproductions with the creator, date, and public-domain basis recorded on each. Three translators have no locatable public-domain portrait, and two portraits await final rights confirmation — those appear as plaques.
blocks.replacement: Sources and rights. Biography highlights are drawn from Skald's three-agent-reviewed translator research. For every portrait shown, the card records its source or collection, creator and date when known, and the stated rights basis. Nineteen portraits are shown; three translators have no locatable public-domain portrait, and two additional portraits are withheld pending confirmation of U.S. public-domain status. These five cards use plaques.
blocks.reason: The review registry supports the three-agent-review claim. The existing sentence overstates the legal status of every served portrait file: the research includes mixed or qualified rights bases, and two unshipped portraits specifically lack a verified U.S. public-domain basis. The proposed wording reports the documented basis rather than making a blanket public-domain assertion.

rationale.kicker: R1's factual objection controls. The gallery contains twenty-four translation records, not twenty-four lives: Butcher–Lang credits two people, and the Pope record also credits Fenton and Broome. 'Twenty-four translations' is exact and keeps the line compact.
rationale.h1: Both reviewers accepted this heading; it is copied verbatim from the page.
rationale.lede: R1 controls the collaboration count and the nineteen-portrait/five-plaque rights breakdown; R2 controls the warmer card, meeting, and version language. The unsupported occupational shorthand and misleading archive metaphor are removed.
rationale.ctaHeading: Both reviewers accepted the heading; it is copied verbatim from the page.
rationale.ctaBody: R2's concrete reader-tool list wins because the facts allow it. Naming the translations, fleet, glossary, and museum art is clearer than 'the margins alive.'
rationale.methodNote: R1 controls the rights wording: the copy does not make a blanket public-domain claim and distinguishes three unlocated portraits from two withheld pending U.S. confirmation. R2's plainer process wording and explicit plaque sentence improve reader clarity without weakening those facts.
